Heard learned Senior Counsel, Mr. M. Mishra instructed by learned counsel, Mr. L. Mishra for the petitioner and learned counsel, Mr. Nayak for the OPID.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Case No.17(A) of 2015, pending on the file of the learned Presiding Officer, Designated Court, Cuttack (under the OPID Act, 2011), arising out of Odisha, EOW, CID, Crime Branch P.S. 3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Presiding Officer, Designated Court, Cuttack, by order dated 31.03.2023 in the aforementioned case,
the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel that the petitioner is in custody since 17.10.2022 on the allegation that one Ambitious Diversified Projects Management Ltd collected money unauthorizedly and later on the same was diversified to one Jetex Ocenair Pvt Ltd of which the petitioner is one of the Directors and is an authorized signatory.

5. It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. L. Mishra for the petitioner that since charge sheet has been filed on 07.02.2023 and the case has not gone beyond the stage of Jaideep Raha vs State Of Odisha .... sentences.text: Keeping in view the nature of allegations and release of the co-accused, the petitioner may be released on bail.

6. Learned counsel for the OPID, Mr. Nayak opposes the prayer for bail and submits that since it's an economic offence the same has to be dealt with on a different scale and merely because charge sheet has been filed, the petitioner who is also a flight risk ought not to be released on bail.

7. A memo has been filed at the behest of the petitioner indicating that the co-accused persons have since been released on bail by this Court by order dated 19.03.2019 in BLAPL No.397 of 2019 by furnishing cash/property security to the tune of Rs.25,00,000/-
7(A).
The other co-accused on Kunal Tiwary was released on by order dated 23.08.2017 in BLAPL No.2564 of 2017 on furnishing cash security to the tune of Rs.25,00,000/- 7(B).

One Omkar Singh was released by order dated 13.11.2017 in BLAPL No.933 of 2017 by furnishing cash security to the tune of Rs.50,00,000/-
7(C).

One Mriganka Sekhar Chakraborty was released by order dated 30.01.2019 in BLAPL No.7162 of 2018 by furnishing property security of Rs.10,00,000/-.
8.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner be put to terms and released inter alia on the ground of parity.

9. The apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation &
Another

entities.text:
Satender Kumar Antil vrs. Central Bureau of Investigation &
Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , reported in 2022 (10) SCC 51 has formulated the guidelines governing the law relating to consideration of bail application.
In the said judgment Economic Offences have been treated as a "class" by itself.

10. The apex Court in catena of Judgments, while generally deprecating the practice of the Courts imposing cash security as a condition precedent for release, a departure has been made in the case of economic offences and that too when public money is involved.

11. Following the said dictum, since the case at hand is an economic offence and taking into account the release of the co- accused and keeping in view the dictum of the apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (Supra) that "uniformity and certainty in the decisions of the Court are the foundations of the judicial dispensation.
Persons accused with the same offence shall never be treated differently either by the same Court or by the same or different Courts (Emphasis).

Such an action though by an exercise of discretion despite being a judicial one would be a grave affront to Article 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India", this Court directs the petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin so as to ensure the presence of the petitioner on each date of trial.

12. The allegation qua the petitioner in paragraph-18.15 of the charge sheet adverted to hereinabove is extracted hereunder:-

sentences.text: 2 "Investigation further surfaced that there was huge diversion of funds during 2011-2012 from the Accounts of M/s Ambitious Diversified Projects Management Ltd maintained with different banks to the accounts of one M/s Jetex Oceanair Pvt.Ltd.
Onscrutiny

, it was found that an amount of Rs 7,00,000/-has been transferred to the HDFC bank A/C No-00282380000039 of Jetex Oceanair Pvt. Ltd. from the Axis bank A/c No-9001020026725898 of ADPM Ltd on 15.02.2012.

An amount of Rs.90,
88,500/-has also been transferred to A/C No- 95001010004964 of M/s Jetex Oceanair Ltd. maintained with Syndicate bank from bank of India A/c No-403520110000182 of ADPM Ltd on different dates.

Further an amount of Rs 85,
45,974 was found to have been transferred from the A/c no-05932560001383 of ADPM Ltd to the A/c 31103935529 of M/s Jetex Oceanair Pt. Ltd. maintained in SBI.
As such, the total amount of Rs.1, 83, 34,474/- was found to have been transferred to the Accounts of M/s Jetex Oceanair Pt. Ltd during the period 2011-2012.
Further, the money trail from the account of M/s JetexOceanair Ltd. has been verified in respect of the above noted amount of Rs.1,83,34,474/-.
On verification of money trail, it was found that no bulk amount has been transferred to the account of any entity or individual.

Investigation also revealed that accused Jaideep Raha (DIN No-00734035) and others are the Directors of Jetex Oceanair (CIN No.
U63090WB1996PTC077529).
Jaideep Raha is also the authorized signatory of Bank accounts of M/s Jetex Oceanair Pvt. Ltd.

Notice has been issued to Jaydeep Raha to appear before I.O for clarification and production of documents for the purpose of fund transferred from Ambitious Diversified Projects Management Ltd. to Jetex ocenair Pvt Ltd. on 14.10.2019 vide letter No-6050/EOW and subsequent dates, but he did not turn up."
13. Taking into account the said allegation, it is directed that the petitioner shall furnish cash security to the tune of Rs.50,00,000/-(Rupees fifty lakhs) before release.
The same shall be kept in an interest bearing account pledged in favour of the learned Court in seisin and shall abide by the final outcome of the case at hand.

14. It is directed that the petitioner shall furnish unencumbered property security to the tune Rs.50,00,000/-(Rupees fifty lakhs) to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin which shall abide by the final outcome.

15. It is needless to state here that both the cash security and the property security as directed does not in any way reflect the complicity of the petitioner and the same has to be adjudicated independently in the impending trial.
16.

It is further directed that if there is any default in appearance as stipulated, it shall be open to the learned Court in seisin to initiate action in accordance with law, without any further reference to this Court.

17. It is further directed that in addition to the sureties so fixed, one surety shall be immediate member of the family, who shall execute a P.R. bond and the petitioner shall furnish his address and Jaideep Raha vs State Of Odisha ....
